report.tagline: A camera-first messaging app where friends send disappearing photos, use AR lenses and watch short videos.
report.simpleSummary: Snapchat opens straight to the camera. You take a photo or video, add a funny filter (called a Lens), and send it to friends, and it disappears after they view it. It also has Stories, a map of where friends are, short videos called Spotlight, and an AI chatbot. It is free and makes most money from ads, but a growing share comes from Snapchat+ subscriptions.

overview.whatItDoes: Snapchat is a visual messaging app. Its main use is sending 'Snaps' (photos and videos) to close friends, often many times a day to keep 'Streaks' going. Around that it adds Stories, Spotlight short videos, Snap Map, AR Lenses and My AI.
howItWorks: The app opens to the camera, so making a Snap is the first thing you do.
You add Lenses, filters or text and send it to friends or post to your Story.
Snaps disappear after viewing by default, which makes sharing feel casual and private.
Between Stories and Spotlight videos, Snap shows ads; advertisers also buy sponsored Lenses.
Snapchat+ (about ₹49 to ₹99 a month in India, $3.99 in the US) gives extra features like custom icons, Story rewatch info and priority My AI.
overview.valueProposition: A fun, low-pressure way to talk to close friends with pictures instead of text, without everything being saved forever.

businessModel.summary: Snapchat makes most money from ads shown between Stories and Spotlight videos, plus sponsored Lenses. Subscriptions are the fastest growing part. Revenue per user is high in North America but very low in India and other markets where most new users come from.

revenueStreams.detail: Ads in Stories, Spotlight and Discover; grew only 4% in Q3 2026.
Snapchat+, Lens+ and Memories Storage; 30 million+ subscribers.
Brands pay for AR try-on and branded effects.
Specs AR glasses at $2,200, not yet significant.

businessModel.pricing: Free app. Snapchat+ $3.99 a month in the US; lower in India. Memories Storage plans for saved Snaps.
businessModel.unitEconomics: Rough estimate. A North American user brings about $11 a quarter, or $44 a year. A Rest of World user, including India, brings about $1.13 a quarter, or under $5 a year. Hosting and serving a user costs a few dollars a year. So Snap earns well on North American users and barely covers costs on many others. Most new users come from markets that pay little, which is why subscriptions matter.

growth.moat: Snapchat is where many young people's close friends are, and it opens to the camera. That close-friend graph and the daily Streak habit are hard to copy. Instagram copied Stories, but Snap remains the main messaging app for many teens.

pmLessons: A strong habit like Streaks keeps users, but it can feel like pressure. Design habits that feel good.
User growth in low-paying markets does not grow revenue much. Subscriptions can help.
Your best feature can be copied (Stories), so keep inventing (Lenses, AR).
Safety and regulation can cut users overnight, as Australia showed.
